jobs.excerpt: OVERVIEWCompass Charter School welcomes dedicated and mission-aligned individuals to serve on our Board of Trustees.
jobs.description:
OVERVIEW

Compass Charter School welcomes dedicated and mission-aligned individuals to serve on our Board of Trustees. We recruit two types of board members: voting members, who hold full governance authority and fiduciary responsibility, and nonvoting family/parent members, who bring the family perspective to board deliberations. All prospective board members, regardless of type, go through a structured process designed to ensure strong fit, transparency, and compliance with New York State Education Department (NYSED) requirements.

SHARED EXPECTATIONS FOR ALL BOARD MEMBERS

All board members, voting and nonvoting, are expected to:

▪ Attend and actively participate in all regularly scheduled board meetings.

▪ Uphold Compass's mission, values, and commitment to progressive, sustainability-focused education.

▪ Maintain confidentiality of executive session discussions.

▪ Disclose any conflicts of interest promptly and recuse when appropriate.

▪ Complete any required board training.

▪ Act in the best interest of Compass students and the school community as a whole.

PARENT BOARD MEMBERS

Parent members are current Compass families who join the board in an advisory capacity, bringing the community perspective to board discussions. To be eligible, a nonvoting family/parent member must have a currently enrolled child at Compass Charter School.

Step 1: Expression of Interest

▪ Families are invited to express interest in a parent board seat through an open call communicated via ParentSquare and school communications.

▪ Interested parents or guardians submit a brief statement of interest and are encouraged to connect with the School Leader or Board Chair with any questions.

Step 2: Application

▪ Interested parents complete an application through Team Tailor.

▪ The application includes a short personal statement and any relevant background the applicant wishes to share.

▪ After reviewing applications, the Executive Committee identifies and advances candidates for further consideration, seeking to build a board that reflects a diversity of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives to strengthen the school's governance and mission.

Step 3: Vetting

▪ The candidate meets with at least two board members and the School Leader.

▪ Conversations focus on the candidate's connection to the Compass community, interest in school governance, and understanding of the nonvoting advisory role.

▪ The Board Development Working Group coordinates scheduling and feedback.

Step 4: Board Approval

▪ The Board Development Working Group presents the candidate to the full board.

▪ The board votes to approve the appointment of the nonvoting parent member for a one-year term.

SY2026–27 Timeline (Current Year Exception)

As this process is being adopted in July 2026, the standard March–June timeline is not applicable for the current year. The following adjusted timeline applies for seating the inaugural voting parent member(s) for SY2026–27:

Late July 2026: Open call launched following the July 28th board meeting. Families are notified of the parent board seat opportunity via ParentSquare and school communications.

November 1 2026: Application period has been extended. Interested families complete an application through Team Tailor. The application deadline is November 1, 2026.

November 2026: Applications reviewed and vetting conversations scheduled. Each advancing candidate meets with at least two board members and the School Leader.

December 2026: Board vote. The full board votes to approve the parent member(s) at the December board meeting. The appointment takes effect immediately upon approval.

Beginning in March 2027, the standard annual recruitment timeline will apply.

jobs.title: Manager, Financial Planning and Analysis & Revenue Operations
jobs.excerpt: Point B helps organizations adapt and thrive as technology, AI, and constant disruption reshape how work gets done.
jobs.description:
Point B helps organizations adapt and thrive as technology, AI, and constant disruption reshape how work gets done. For more than 30 years, we’ve connected strategy, execution, and technology so teams, systems, and decisions can move together under pressure. This work helps clients drive growth, improve operational efficiency, and accelerate time to value. We don’t stop at recommendations. We stay with the work through delivery to turn plans into measurable progress and lasting results.

JOB SUMMARY

    We are seeking an analytical, execution-oriented Finance Manager, Revenue Operations & FP&A to own the processes, systems, and analytics that make Point B’s revenue predictable and our performance visible. Roughly 70% of the role is Revenue Operations: pipeline governance, forecasting operations, Salesforce, and account-planning infrastructure. The remaining 30% is FP&A: annual planning, forecasting, cost planning, and variance analysis.

    Point B’s revenue is won through relationships, delivered by consultants on client assignments, and grown through long-term client partnerships. Revenue performance therefore depends on pipeline quality, how quickly sold work becomes staffed assignments, and consultant utilization, not subscription metrics. The successful candidate develops recommendations, executes agreed priorities, and partners closely with market and practice leaders, Business Development, Marketing, Finance, Accounting, Resource Management, and Delivery Operations to create one shared source of truth from opportunity to revenue.

RESPONSIBILITIES

    Revenue Operations Responsibilities

    • Own Point B’s pipeline management process, cadence, and reporting, including recurring pipeline reviews with market, practice, and business development leadership.

    • Own the pipeline-based bookings and revenue forecast in partnership with the Business Apps team and Finance, translating open opportunities into expected bookings and revenue timing so leadership can see how pipeline converts into staffed work.

    • Coach sellers and practice leaders on pipeline hygiene, including stage, probability, close date, estimated start date, and engagement value, to improve forecast accuracy.

    • Monitor bookings, pipeline coverage against revenue targets, win rates, and conversion trends, and flag risks and opportunities to leadership.

    • Build and maintain Salesforce dashboards, reports, and account-level views that give sellers and leaders self-service visibility into client metrics such as YTD revenue, bookings, open pipeline, and active assignments.

    • Maintain alignment between Salesforce and downstream financial and resourcing data so that pipeline, bookings, and revenue reconcile.

    • Own the tools, process, reporting, and enablement for account planning and key-client management.

    • Streamline the opportunity-to-assignment lifecycle, including opportunity management, proposal development, SOWs and contracting, handoffs to staffing and delivery, and account expansion.

    • Maintain leadership KPIs and analytics on utilization, bill rates, margins, and client performance, combining Salesforce with financial and resourcing data.

    FP&A Responsibilities

    • Manage annual planning data, models, process, and deliverables, partnering with market and practice leaders and Resource Management on revenue, headcount, role-based utilization, and capacity assumptions and targets.

    • Incorporate the pipeline forecast into monthly and quarterly financial forecasts, compare them to actuals, explain variances, and recommend actions.

    • Perform scenario and sensitivity analysis on key drivers such as bookings, utilization, bill rates, and headcount to show leadership the range of potential outcomes.

    • Support G&A and operating cost budgeting, including aligning cost plans to revenue scenarios and tracking actions against plan.

    • Support pricing governance and business performance reviews.

    • Streamline recurring FP&A processes and work with IT and Business Apps to automate reporting where possible.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

    • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Economics, Analytics, or a related field

    • 5-7+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, FP&A, Business Unit Finance, or Consulting Operations, with hands-on exposure to both revenue operations and financial planning

    • Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills, including forecasting, scenario analysis, and variance analysis

    • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex financial and operational information simply to executives

    • Experience managing cross-functional initiatives and process improvements

    • A hands-on, detail-oriented approach that balances accuracy with urgency

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

    • Experience with Salesforce CRM, including reports, dashboards, data governance, sales process design, and configuration; Salesforce Administrator certification a plus

    • Experience with Power BI, including data models, DAX, and report development; Tableau or other BI experience also considered

    • Experience in professional services, management consulting, technology consulting, or another project-based services organization, including working knowledge of utilization, bill rates, staffing-driven revenue, and professional services automation (PSA) or resource management systems

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS:

    The estimated salary range for this role is $XX - $XX USD per year. This salary range is provided as required by local and state law as applicable. Individual salaries vary on a number of factors including but not limited to geography, skills, education, experience and unique qualifications where applicable.
    Bonuses are awarded at Point B’s discretion and are based upon individual contributions and overall firm performance.
    Employees hired on or after October 1 are not eligible to participate in the current year’s bonus or merit increase cycle. Eligibility will begin with the following performance cycle, in accordance with company policy.

Intrigued To Learn More?

At Point B, you’ll own meaningful work from day one, contribute your perspective, and stay connected to the outcomes you help create. As you build expertise through hands-on experience, coaches and leaders will support your growth and help you take on what’s next. Point B also offers flexible work options and competitive benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k), paid time off, paid sick leave, and an employee assistance program, within a culture consistently recognized as one of the best places to work.

jobs.description:
About Summit:

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.

Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:

Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

  • HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.

  • HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

  • HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC)

  • HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland.

Overview of Role:

Serves as the project level biostatistician and provides leadership within biostatistics function to develop and execute statistical strategy, study design, statistical analyses, and regulatory submissions for clinical trials in oncology. Partners with clinical science, regulatory and other team members in clinical development plans, authoring key clinical/regulatory/statistical documents, and ensuring exceptional delivery and interpretation of clinical data. Develops and implements biostatistics department policies, standards, procedures, and work-instructions in coordination with department leader and other functions. Represents biostatistics function in interactions with CROs, institutional review boards, and regulatory agencies.

Role and Responsibilities:

  • Provide technical leadership and statistical support to clinical development through the design and conduct of clinical studies in oncology
  • Support/contribute to protocol development to ensure appropriateness of trial design, sample size, and propose the use of meaningful and efficient statistical methodologies
  • Lead development of statistical analysis plans, data presentation plans, clinical development plans, biometrics related submission activities, and post-submission strategies/responses
  • Review the accuracy of clinical data, perform statistical analysis, interpret study results, and collaborate with clinical team and other team members to produce interim reports, final reports, and publications
  • Write/review sections of meeting packages and assist in the development and review of other documents required for regulatory submissions and other regulatory processes
  • Review vendor data transfer specifications and ADaM programming specifications
  • Lead assessment and introduction of novel statistical methodologies to implement solutions
  • Represent biostatistics function or biometrics department in cross function teams
  • Work with department leader to develop and implement department policies, standards and procedures
  • Collaborate with clinical operations, data management and CRO to develop and implement CRFs, database design, and the overall data quality plan
  • Evaluate and manage CROs and other vendors, including scope-of-work, timelines, deliverables and budgets
  • Provide strategic statistical and regulatory guidance to anticipate challenges, mitigate risk, and ensure project success
  • Attend meetings with FDA or other health authorities to ensure ongoing agreement on project development
  • All other duties as assigned

Experience, Education and Specialized Knowledge and Skills:

  • Ph.D. in Statistics, Biostatistics or equivalent area with 6+ years biopharmaceutical industry experience required. MS degree in related discipline with extensive industry and leadership experience (8+ years) can be considered.
  • Strong proficiencies in software and other tools typically used by Biostatistics (e.g. SAS, R)
  • Good understanding of clinical trial processes and statistical programming requirements
  • Working knowledge of ICH, FDA and GCP regulations and guidelines
  • Attention to detail, accuracy and confidentiality
  • Clear and concise oral and written communication skills
  • Must be able to effectively multi-task and manage time-sensitive and highly confidential documents.
  • Communicate effectively and articulate complex ideas in an easily understandable way
  • Work in a fast-paced, demanding and collaborative environment

This is the pay for this position

Pay Transparency
$174,000—$203,000 USD

This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor. jobs.excerpt: Who We AreFlosum is a bootstrapped, profitable B2B SaaS company building the leading Salesforce-native DevSecOps, Data Protection, and Security platform.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Flosum is a bootstrapped, profitable B2B SaaS company building the leading Salesforce-native DevSecOps, Data Protection, and Security platform. Our solutions are trusted by Fortune 500 enterprises in the most heavily regulated industries on the planet — financial services, healthcare, government, and insurance.

We’re not a startup burning cash and chasing vanity metrics. We’re a proven, scaling business that reached profitability on our own terms. As a Salesforce Summit Partner and Innovation Award winner, we’ve earned our seat at the table alongside the biggest names in enterprise software.

Built 100% on the Salesforce platform. Serving enterprises that demand zero compromise on security, compliance, and reliability.

Why This Role Exists

We are entering an aggressive growth phase — expanding our product surface, deepening our platform capabilities, and accelerating our delivery velocity. We need senior-caliber Node.js developers who can own significant parts of our architecture and ship production code that enterprise customers depend on daily.

This is not a staff augmentation seat. You will work directly with engineering leadership, product managers, and the CEO. Your decisions will have real consequences, your opinions will be heard, and your craftsmanship will be visible to the customers who rely on our platform.

What You’ll Build

  • High-performance backend services and APIs powering enterprise-grade SaaS applications
  • Scalable, secure Node.js micro services and integrations within the Salesforce ecosystem
  • Modern front-end experiences using Vue.js and TypeScript that serve demanding enterprise users
  • CI/CD pipeline tooling, automation frameworks, and developer productivity infrastructure
  • Real-time data processing and event-driven architectures handling sensitive enterprise data at scale

Requirements

Read this section carefully. We are specific about what we need because we are serious about who we hire.

Non-Negotiable Technical Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional Node.js development in production environments — not tutorials, not side projects, not bootcamp exercises. Real production systems serving real users at scale.
  • Expert-level understanding of asynchronous programming, event loops, streams, and the Node.js runtime. You should be able to explain backpressure, the differences between setImmediate and process.nextTick, and why unhandled promise rejections are dangerous — without Googling it.
  • Deep experience with TypeScript in production codebases. We write typed code, and we expect you to understand why.
  • Strong command of RESTful API design, authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT), and API security best practices for enterprise environments.
  • Proven experience with SQL and NoSQL databases, query optimization, data modeling, and understanding the performance implications of schema decisions at scale.
  • Proficiency with Git workflows, code review practices, automated testing (unit, integration, and end-to-end), and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Solid understanding of containerization (Docker), cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure), and infrastructure-as-code principles.

Highly Preferred (These Will Set You Apart)

  • Salesforce development experience: Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Visualforce, or Salesforce API integrations. If you know both Node.js and Salesforce, you are a rare and extremely valuable candidate to us.
  • Experience building or contributing to Salesforce ISV (AppExchange) products.
  • Vue.js front-end development experience, particularly with Vue 3 Composition API and state management.
  • Experience working in B2B SaaS companies serving enterprise customers with strict compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR).
  • Familiarity with DevOps/DevSecOps toolchains and practices in the Salesforce ecosystem.

The Kind of Person We’re Looking For

Skills get you in the door. Mindset determines whether you thrive here:

Missionary, Not Mercenary

You care about what you’re building and why. You take ownership not because someone assigned it to you, but because that’s who you are. When something is broken at 2 AM, you don’t check whether it’s “your responsibility” — you fix it.

Builder, Not a Bystander

You don’t wait for perfect specifications. You dig in, ask hard questions, propose solutions, and ship. You would rather have a working prototype by Friday than a polished slide deck by next quarter.

Craftsperson Under Pressure

Enterprise customers depend on our uptime and data integrity. You write code that doesn’t just work — it survives. You understand that in regulated industries, your code is your reputation.

Direct Communicator

You say what you think, respectfully and clearly. If a technical decision is wrong, you speak up — regardless of who made it. We value candor over politeness-at-the-expense-of-quality.

This Is a Long-Term Commitment

Let us be direct: we are not looking for contractors who jump between projects every few months. We are building a world-class engineering team, and we invest heavily in the people who join us. In return, we expect commitment.

This role is designed as a long-term, full-time engagement. You will grow with us. You will own systems end-to-end. You will see the direct impact of your work in how Fortune 500 companies build, protect, and deploy on Salesforce.

If you’re looking for a short-term gig while you wait for something else, this isn’t the role. If you want to build something that matters and be part of a team that’s scaling from strong to dominant, keep reading.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with your experience and impact
  • Direct collaboration with the founding team and engineering leadership — your voice will carry weight from day one
  • A profitable, stable company with aggressive growth plans — no funding anxiety, no runway clock
  • The opportunity to work on enterprise-grade products used by some of the largest organizations in the world
  • Meaningful technical challenges: security, compliance, scale, and reliability at the intersection of Node.js and Salesforce
  • A culture that rewards ownership, speed, and craftsmanship over politics and hierarchy
  • Remote-first flexibility with a results-oriented work environment

JumpCloud® is the AI-powered unified IT management platform designed to secure the modern workforce. JumpCloud is Intelligent, Secure IT.

About the Role:

The Senior Manager, Direct Sales leads JumpCloud's Commercial Direct Sales team (5–7 Account Executives) responsible for acquiring new logos and expanding market footprint within organizations of 100 to 1,000 employees. As JumpCloud scales, this leader solves the critical business need for a structured, high-velocity outbound pipeline generation engine that drives predictable Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR). By embedding daily AI-driven sales workflows, rigorous MEDDPICC qualification, and data-backed Gong coaching cadences, you will lead a proven team of high performers through organizational transitions into their next phase of growth.
Reporting directly to the VP of Global Sales, you will turn strategic growth priorities into consistent quarterly execution, driving new customer acquisition and market leadership.

Employee Value Proposition

  • Purpose: Champion JumpCloud’s core growth engine by empowering commercial enterprises to securely unify identity, access, and device management in the modern AI age.

  • Growth: Own the commercial territory strategy, pilot cutting-edge AI-native prospecting methodologies, and elevate high-caliber Account Executives into top enterprise sales performers and future leaders.

  • Motivators: Lead a President's Club-caliber team with substantial executive visibility, shape channel and alliance co-selling strategies, and build a lasting impact on JumpCloud’s flagship sales segment.

Major Performance Objectives

    Measurable outcomes for the first 6-12 months:

    1. Deliver 100%+ of Team Quota Attainment: Achieve the team roll-up revenue target by coaching and managing 5–7 Account Executives to consistently hit and exceed individual quarterly quotas within the first 6–12 months.

    2. Establish a Predictable Outbound Pipeline Motion: Design and scale a repeatable outbound hunting framework that increases rep-generated outbound pipeline by at least 35% within the first 6 months, mitigating reliance on inbound channels.

    3. Operationalize Daily AI Prospecting Adoption: Embed daily generative and predictive AI workflows across the entire sales team within 90 days, demonstrating measurable gains in outbound sequencing velocity, account research depth, and conversion speed.

    5. Scale Channel & Partner-Sourced Pipeline: Collaborate with Alliances and Channel Partners to integrate partner co-selling motions into commercial territory plans, generating at least 20% of new commercial pipeline via partner channels within the first 12 months.

Critical Subtasks

    Supporting activities to achieve objectives (order logically):

    1. Evaluate current territory distribution, pipeline coverage ratios, and historical conversion metrics across the commercial direct sales segment.

    2. Develop, test, and roll out standardized outbound sales plays, messaging sequences, and multi-touch cadences utilizing Outreach and LinkedIn Sales Navigator.

    3. Integrate daily AI tools into standard rep workflows to streamline target account research, craft personalized outreach, and surface deal risk early.

    4. Implement weekly structured 1:1 coaching and deal review sessions utilizing Gong call recordings and MEDDPICC frameworks to upskill reps and remove pipeline blockers.

    5. Manage and deliver precise weekly, monthly, and quarterly ARR forecasts in Salesforce, maintaining continuous alignment with executive sales leadership.

    6. Partner cross-functionally with Channel/Alliances, Sales Enablement, and Product Marketing to align territory co-selling, campaign execution, and competitive positioning.

    7. Mentor, retain, and recruit high-performing sales talent, maintaining high team morale, accountability, and professional growth during structural and organizational shifts.

Skills and Experience

    Must-have functional skills:

  • Proven track record of managing and leading quota-carrying B2B SaaS direct sales teams to consistent target achievement.

  • Demonstrated success in designing and executing outbound hunting motions, pipeline generation playbooks, and territory build-outs.

  • Mastery of structured sales qualification frameworks (MEDDPICC) and conversational intelligence deal inspection.

  • Proven leadership in sales coaching—diagnosing performance gaps, coaching both underperformers and top performers, and driving accountability with empathy.

  • Experience integrating channel, reseller, and ecosystem partners into active direct sales cycles.

    • Preferred domain knowledge:

  • Commercial B2B SaaS sales segment (100–1,000 employees) and understanding of IT, DevOps, and Security buyer personas.

  • Identity and Access Management (IAM), cloud directory services, or cybersecurity infrastructure software.

  • Experience managing sales motions or expanding territories in Latin America (LATAM) is a plus.

    • Tools or systems knowledge:

  • Salesforce (SFDC) for opportunity management, pipeline analytics, and executive ARR forecasting.

  • Gong (or equivalent conversation intelligence platforms) for structured call analysis, scorecards, and deal coaching.

  • Outreach, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, or modern sales engagement tech stacks.

  • Hands-on daily utilization of AI tools for prospecting, content personalization, and workflow acceleration.

    • Behavioral or power skills:

  • Empathetic yet accountable leadership style capable of steering high-performing teams through organizational change.

  • Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret sales metrics, diagnose pipeline trends, and implement decisive execution plans.

  • Exceptional cross-functional communication and stakeholder management across all leadership levels.

  • High-conviction, curious, and resilient attitude suited for high-growth environments.

In accordance with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, the approximate annual compensation range for this role, depending on individual candidate level and experience, is $200,000 - $265,000 OTE, including base salary and any related bonuses or commissions.

In the US, JumpCloud® provides a comprehensive benefits package, with several medical plans to choose from including a high deductible HSA plan with employer contribution, two dental plans, vision insurance, flexible spending account (FSA), employee assistance program (EAP), short- and long-term disability, life insurance and a 401k savings plan with match. We have a flexible paid time off policy.

Where you’ll be working/Location:

JumpCloud® is committed to being Remote First, meaning that you are able to work remotely within the country noted in the Job Description.
All roles posted in United States locations do require that you be located within one of the 50 U.S. States. Our Headquarters is in the Denver/Boulder, CO area but as a remote company, you are able to work remotely anywhere in the U.S. If you would like to spend time in our offices in the Denver/Boulder area, you are welcome to do that as well.

Language:

JumpCloud® has teams in 15+ countries around the world and conducts our internal business in English. The interview and any additional screening process will take place primarily in English. To be considered for a role at JumpCloud®, you will be required to speak and write in English fluently. Any additional language requirements will be included in the details of the job description.

Why JumpCloud?

If you thrive working in a fast, SaaS-based environment and you are passionate about solving challenging technical problems, we look forward to hearing from you! JumpCloud® is an incredible place to share and grow your expertise! You’ll work with amazing talent across each department who are passionate about our mission. We’re out of the box thinkers, so your unique ideas and approaches for conceiving a product and/or feature will be welcome. You’ll have a voice in the organization as you work with a seasoned executive team, a supportive board and in a proven market that our customers are excited about.
One of JumpCloud®'s three core values is to “Build Connections.” To us that means creating " human connection with each other regardless of our backgrounds, orientations, geographies, religions, languages, gender, race, etc. We care deeply about the people that we work with and want to see everyone succeed." - Rajat Bhargava, CEO
Please submit your résumé and brief explanation about yourself and why you would be a good fit for JumpCloud®. Please note JumpCloud® is not accepting third party resumes at this time.
JumpCloud® is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

Scam Notice:

Please be aware that there are individuals and organizations that may attempt to scam job seekers by offering fraudulent employment opportunities in the name of JumpCloud. These scams may involve fake job postings, unsolicited emails, or messages claiming to be from our recruiters or hiring managers. Walden University seeks a dynamic, innovative faculty member for this contributing (part-time) position in the Ph.D. in Social Work and the DSW programs. Key responsibilities of this position include teaching courses and mentoring student research.

What to Expect as a Walden Faculty Member

Faculty members educate Walden University students by effectively and proficiently using online technology and resources so that knowledge, information, feedback, and critique are imparted to and shared with students in thoughtful, carefully formulated, well written, and timely communications. This is accomplished in an environment that is respectful of the student, the faculty member, Walden University, and the discipline in which the faculty member is involved.

Course Teaching/Availability

Faculty members are assigned courses, which are taught using the Learning Management System (LMS), and are responsible for interacting with students within the LMS. Discussion Boards for classrooms are open 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. Faculty members are expected to be in the classroom a minimum of 4 days per week and responses to student questions must be posted within 48 hours. The university suggests regular and predictable availability, such as online office hours or regular online chats; office hours may be required based on program or college policy.

Research Mentorship

Faculty mentors may be assigned to work one-on-one with students to help students meet the research requirements of their degree. Faculty members are responsible for the provision of timely feedback, approval, assessment, and evaluation of each student's work within the classroom.

Residencies

Graduate-level faculty may be invited to attend Residencies held domestically or internationally, where they will teach face-to-face intensives and colloquia, and facilitate school and university-wide discussions. Contributing (part-time) faculty may be invited to participate but are not required to attend.

Tools/Technical Skills

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Incumbents will be evaluated, in part, based on performance of each essential function. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Licensing/Certification

Faculty members must be appropriately credentialed, possess an earned degree from an accredited institution or an institution that is recognized by a country's ministry of education in the discipline being taught, and may be expected to be licensed or license-eligible in order to teach in specific programs. Faculty members must maintain their licenses and any appropriate certifications in order to continue to teach at Walden University. Faculty members are also expected to maintain currency with research by reviewing articles, journals, and presentations. If participating in research, the faculty member may publish and acknowledge Walden University.

Travel

Contributing faculty members may have the opportunity to travel to university events and residencies. When traveling to these events, the faculty member will be expected to fully participate in the event. For core faculty, there will be required travel throughout the year.

The successful candidate will have:

  • An earned Ph.D. or DSW from an accredited university in social work.
  • MSW from a Council for Social Work Education (CSWE) accredited program.
  • Experience sitting on/chairing dissertation committees
  • Possess a significant record of academic (i.e., publications, presentations) and/or professional contributions to the field of study.
  • A minimum of 3 years of teaching experience at the degree level of the program and one year of online teaching experience is preferred
  • A minimum of 3 years post-MSW social work practice experience.
  • A commitment to supporting student success in a diverse population of adult learners.
  • Have a commitment to the social change mission of Walden University.
  • Experience with Learning Management Systems and leveraging technology in learning (required).
  • Proficiency with SPSS for quantitative faculty and/or NVivo for qualitative faculty, preferred.
  • Be expected to perform other duties and responsibilities that management may deem necessary from time to time.

Technology Requirements

Faculty members are expected to have a personal computer with virus protection and Internet access. Walden University provides a Walden e-mail account and access to the learning platform, password-protected faculty sections of the website, university and college listservs, and other faculty communications tools.

In support of the pay transparency laws enacted across the country, the expected compensation rate for this position is as follows:

  • Graduate Course Instruction: $1,560 - $4,080 per Quarter or Semester, depending on type of course taught and length of course
  • Undergraduate Course Instruction: $700 - $2,200 per quarter, depending on type of course taught and length of course

    Actual pay may be adjusted based on job-related factors permitted by law, such as type of course taught; experience and training; geographic location; licensure and certifications; market factors; departmental budgets; and responsibility. Walden also offers other opportunities for its adjunct faculty members, such as dissertation/doctoral study committee chair positions, research reviewing, and dissertation and doctoral study mentoring.

Equal Opportunity – Minority / Female / Disability / V / Gender Identity / Sexual Orientation

Walden

More than 50 years ago, Walden University was founded to support adult learners in achieving their academic goals and making a greater impact in their professions and communities. Students from across the U.S. and more than 90 countries are pursuing a certificate, bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral degree online at Walden. We offer more than 100 online degrees and certificate programs. Walden University is accredited by The Higher Learning Commission ().   • Salesforce development experience: Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Visualforce, or Salesforce API integrations. If you know both Node.js and Salesforce, you are a rare and extremely valuable candidate to us.
  • Experience building or contributing to Salesforce ISV (AppExchange) products.
  • Vue.js front-end development experience, particularly with Vue 3 Composition API and state management.
  • Experience working in B2B SaaS companies serving enterprise customers with strict compliance requirements (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR).
  • Familiarity with DevOps/DevSecOps toolchains and practices in the Salesforce ecosystem.

The Kind of Person We’re Looking For

Skills get you in the door. Mindset determines whether you thrive here:

Missionary, Not Mercenary

You care about what you’re building and why. You take ownership not because someone assigned it to you, but because that’s who you are. When something is broken at 2 AM, you don’t check whether it’s “your responsibility” — you fix it.

Builder, Not a Bystander

You don’t wait for perfect specifications. You dig in, ask hard questions, propose solutions, and ship. You would rather have a working prototype by Friday than a polished slide deck by next quarter.

Craftsperson Under Pressure

Enterprise customers depend on our uptime and data integrity. You write code that doesn’t just work — it survives. You understand that in regulated industries, your code is your reputation.

Direct Communicator

You say what you think, respectfully and clearly. If a technical decision is wrong, you speak up — regardless of who made it. We value candor over politeness-at-the-expense-of-quality.

This Is a Long-Term Commitment

Let us be direct: we are not looking for contractors who jump between projects every few months. We are building a world-class engineering team, and we invest heavily in the people who join us. In return, we expect commitment.

This role is designed as a long-term, full-time engagement. You will grow with us. You will own systems end-to-end. You will see the direct impact of your work in how Fortune 500 companies build, protect, and deploy on Salesforce.

If you’re looking for a short-term gig while you wait for something else, this isn’t the role. If you want to build something that matters and be part of a team that’s scaling from strong to dominant, keep reading.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with your experience and impact
  • Direct collaboration with the founding team and engineering leadership — your voice will carry weight from day one
  • A profitable, stable company with aggressive growth plans — no funding anxiety, no runway clock
  • The opportunity to work on enterprise-grade products used by some of the largest organizations in the world
  • Meaningful technical challenges: security, compliance, scale, and reliability at the intersection of Node.js and Salesforce

The Design Manager is responsible for leading and managing the technical design function within the practice. This role oversees a team of Design Leads and design staff, ensuring work is properly assigned, resources are effectively utilized, and project deliverables meet established quality and design standards. The Design Manager serves as the steward of design excellence by implementing, maintaining, and enforcing design processes, technical standards, and quality control procedures across all projects.

The Design Manager works closely with Project Managers, Practice Leaders, and Discipline Leaders to ensure consistent delivery, efficient utilization of resources, and high-quality technical outcomes that support organizational goals and client satisfaction.

The Impact You'll Make:

Design Leadership & Team Management

  • Lead, mentor, and develop Design Leads and technical staff.

  • Establish clear performance expectations and accountability measures for design teams.

  • Facilitate staff development, technical growth, and succession planning.

  • Promote collaboration and knowledge sharing among design teams.

  • Support recruiting, onboarding, and retention of design personnel.

  • Manages day-to-day personnel administration of direct reports, including timekeeping, expense approvals, performance evaluations, employee development, and other routine personnel matters in accordance with company policies

Resource Planning & Workload Management

  • Coordinate and balance workload across Design Leads and technical teams.

  • Assign design resources based on project needs, technical capabilities, and staff development objectives.

  • Monitor team utilization and proactively address workload imbalances.

  • Collaborate with Project Managers to forecast staffing needs and identify resource constraints.

Design Standards & Technical Excellence

  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve design standards, procedures, and best practices.

  • Ensure consistent application of organizational CAD, BIM, engineering, and design standards.

  • Lead implementation of technical tools, templates, and standard processes.

  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to increase efficiency and design consistency.

  • Serve as the technical authority for design execution and delivery practices.

Quality Control & Quality Assurance

  • Own and maintain the organization's design quality control program.

  • Establish and enforce QC review procedures and documentation requirements.

  • Conduct periodic audits of project deliverables to verify compliance with standards.

  • Ensure design reviews are completed at established project milestones.

  • Track quality metrics, lessons learned, and corrective actions to continuously improve performance.

  • Foster a culture of quality, accountability, and technical excellence.

Project Delivery Support

  • Partner with Project Managers to support successful project execution.

  • Provide technical oversight on complex or high-risk projects.

  • Assist in resolving technical challenges and design conflicts.

  • Support proposal development, staffing plans, and project execution strategies.

  • Ensure design deliverables align with client requirements, contract obligations, and regulatory standards.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Quality issues and design rework are minimized.

  • Design standards and QC processes are consistently followed.

  • Project deliverables are completed on time.

  • Staff resources are effectively allocated across projects.

  • Technical staff demonstrate growth, engagement, and retention.

  • Design reviews and audits are completed with positive results.

  • Process improvements are implemented and embraced by the team.

Professional Growth & Career Development

The Design Manager role provides a pathway for expanded leadership responsibilities within project delivery and business operations. Individuals in this position are encouraged to develop project management competencies, including project planning, scope management, financial performance, client communication, and risk management.

As part of professional development, Design Managers may:

  • Serve as Deputy Project Managers on complex assignments.

  • Lead internal project delivery initiatives and multidisciplinary coordination efforts.

  • Participate in project financial reviews, forecasting, and resource planning.

  • Support client communications and stakeholder engagement activities.

  • Develop proficiency in project management tools, processes, and best practices.

  • Transition into Project Manager, Senior Project Manager, Operations Leader, or Practice Leadership roles as experience and capabilities expand.

This growth opportunity allows Design Managers to leverage their technical leadership experience while gaining the project delivery and business management skills necessary for broader organizational leadership positions.

A successful Design Manager is a highly respected technical leader who effectively balances people leadership, resource management, quality control, and design excellence. This individual creates accountability, establishes clear design expectations, develops high-performing teams, and ensures every project is delivered in accordance with company standards and client expectations.

Whether you're launching your career or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to work alongside industry-leading experts, collaborate across disciplines and borders, and contribute to projects that transform the way people live, move, and connect. jobs.description:
Senior Program Officer, Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA)

Location: Remote and must be based in a country within our current hiring locations in the Sub-Saharan Africa region

Summary

The Wikimedia Foundation is a non-profit organization supporting Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. The Foundation operates one of the world’s top five websites and has global reach and impact. At the core of the projects are volunteers who curate the knowledge that the world has come to rely on.

The Community Resources team is the primary funding function of the Wikimedia Foundation ensuring that we support the Affiliates and volunteer contributors of the Wikimedia Movement by offering institutional and individual funding to help achieve the Movement’s goals. To support the movement’s commitment to Knowledge Equity, the team prioritizes proactive outreach to communities that structures of power and privilege have left out.

The Senior Program Officer will implement the regional funding programs serving Wikimedian communities in Sub-Saharan Africa.

Roles and Responsibilities

Funding Strategy & Portfolio Management

  • Implement the Community Resources grantmaking strategy while taking into consideration community needs, opportunities, movement trends, and the regional geopolitical and cultural context.
  • Analyze regional and global patterns to shape funding rationales and priorities.
  • Design program activities with colleagues to achieve significant, scalable impact.
  • Manage, implement and monitor the regional grant portfolio to ensure alignment with strategy, criteria, and impact goals.
  • Lead annual grant planning: identify and support prospective and returning grantees, review proposals, co-develop funding rationales with the regional funding committee. This also includes conducting organizational assessments (financial and narrative) to inform funding rationales.
  • Work collaboratively across Foundation teams to support implementation of funding program and team objectives.
  • Represent the Foundation internally and externally as an ambassador for regional knowledge, priorities and insights.

Committee Development

  • Build, onboard, and develop regional funding committees aligned with regional needs and opportunities to enable transparent decision-making as part of participatory grantmaking approaches.
  • Set agendas for committee discussions (priorities, financial analysis, partner and regional insights) and facilitate inclusive funding deliberations.
  • Provide context, analysis, and synthesis of committee feedback into funding recommendations and decisions.
  • Provide constructive feedback to applicants and grantees on outcomes and expectations linked to funding decisions.

Community & Funding Partner Management

  • Build and sustain trust-based relationships with communities, grantees, and applicants across the region; act as primary liaison between WMF and partners.
  • Understand community needs, dynamics, and challenges; support conflict resolution or sensitive discussions when required.
  • Support community, organizational/institutional strengthening of grantee partners; connect them with relevant and needed best practices and resources.
  • Design and support convenings, collaborations, and knowledge sharing to enable learning amongst partners within the portfolio, with the community and ecosystem.
  • Engage regional philanthropic spaces and leaders to strengthen grantee support and advance meaningful and mission-aligned philanthropy practices.

Evaluation and Learning

  • Review grantee progress through conversations, reports, and site visits, and share insight reports.
  • Reviews and approves grant reports, following up when necessary to ensure completeness, discussing concerns, and offering appropriate guidance and support.
  • Identify trends, gaps, and opportunities from grantmaking data to inform the grant strategy, regional priorities, and resource allocation.
  • Share learnings with colleagues, committees, and movement partners; contribute to strategic conversations on resource allocation.

Skills and Experience:

The right person is better than the right set of experiences. These are the traits we’ve identified that make great additions to our team so far.

  • Solid knowledge of trust-based philanthropy or community-based grantmaking;
  • Experience in participatory decision-making structures
  • Experience in grantmaking, particularly in an international context
  • Experience in nonprofit capacity building as a funder, consultant, or nonprofit leader;
  • Strong strategic and analytical skills and creative problem-solving ability;
  • Excellent organizational skills and judgment; ability to prioritize work, manage time and multiple priorities, and meet deadlines; attention to detail and accuracy; the ability to set realistic goals and objectives;
  • Proven ability that would translate to creating constructive partnerships with the Wikimedia community, stakeholders, and fund-seekers: skills in facilitating engaging, motivating, coordinating and supporting volunteer communities, and in negotiating the sometimes chaotic and contentious nature of free-thinking communities
  • An open and transparent communication style; ability to engage and have dialogue with individuals in a public setting and in a non-polarizing way
  • Experience managing high complexity projects and stakeholders
  • Willingness to accommodate scheduling requirements of frequent interactions across time zones, with individuals and organizations across the world
  • Proven English proficiency in written and spoken communication, including speaking in front of large groups and reacting publicly in high-pressure situations, and comfort in producing widely distributed written material
  • Demonstrated commitment to and belief in equity, inclusion, and diversity
  • A global perspective, with significant experience living or working internationally
  • This position may require 1-3 international trips each year when circumstances allow.

Additionally, we’d love it if you have:

  • Experience working with online communities, particularly in the free knowledge movement
  • Passion for or experience contributing to Wikipedia/Wikimedia project
  • Besides English, proficiency in another language would be an added value.

About the Wikimedia Foundation

The Wikimedia Foundation is the nonprofit organization that operates Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia free knowledge projects. Our vision is a world in which every single human can freely share in the sum of all knowledge. We believe that everyone has the potential to contribute something to our shared knowledge, and that everyone should be able to access that knowledge freely. We host Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects, build software experiences for reading, contributing, and sharing Wikimedia content, support the volunteer communities and partners who make Wikimedia possible, and advocate for policies that enable Wikimedia and free knowledge to thrive.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a charitable, not-for-profit organization that relies on donations. We receive donations from millions of individuals around the world, with an average donation of about $15. We also receive donations through institutional grants and gifts. The Wikimedia Foundation is a United States 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization with offices in San Francisco, California, USA.

As an equal opportunity employer, the Wikimedia Foundation values having a diverse workforce and continuously strives to maintain an inclusive and equitable workplace. We encourage people with a diverse range of backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate against any person based upon their race, traits historically associated with race, religion, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy or related medical conditions, parental status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or any other legally protected characteristics.

The Wikimedia Foundation is a remote-first organization with staff members including contractors based 40+ countries*. Salaries at the Wikimedia Foundation are set in a way that is competitive, equitable, and consistent with our values and culture. The anticipated annual pay range of this position for applicants based within the United States is US$85,761 to US$130,513 with multiple individualized factors, including cost of living in the location, being the determinants of the offered pay. For applicants located outside of the US, the pay range will be adjusted to the country of hire. We neither ask for nor take into consideration the salary history of applicants. The compensation for a successful applicant will be based on their skills, experience and location.

GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. Overview

As part of the GPSU program, we are seeking a Cybersecurity Presales Intern to support GuidePoint Security's Heartland region. In this role, you will get hands-on experience in three core areas: certification and technical foundations, presales and client engagement, technical delivery and writing, and vendor knowledge. Experienced practitioners will mentor you directly on real work, not simulations. You don't need prior experience in this exact role, but you do need technical aptitude, a habit of learning on your own, and real curiosity about cybersecurity.

You must be pursuing or have recently completed a Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field. We will also consider Associate's degree candidates who show self-study and lab work. Non-traditional backgrounds are welcome to apply, including career changers, military veterans, and self-taught candidates, as long as they show equivalent knowledge. You will work with the Heartland presales team, shadowing senior consultants on client engagements and attending internal presales and delivery meetings to learn the business. This internship is a pathway to full-time employment. Candidates who show competence and cultural fit may receive a full-time offer, with a growth path to Pre-Sales Cybersecurity Technical Advisor and a long-term path toward CISSP-level certifications and senior advisory roles.

Responsibilities

  • Certification & Technical Foundation
    • Build a certification foundation with company-sponsored exam vouchers, including Security+, Network+, CySA+, and cloud certifications
    • Complete hands-on lab work to strengthen skills in networking, operating systems, cloud, and security
    • Take part in CTF platforms such as HackTheBox and TryHackMe to build practical offensive and defensive skills
    • Gain exposure to SIEM, vulnerability scanning, and endpoint security tools in lab and real-world settings under mentorship
  • Presales & Client Engagement
    • Shadow senior consultants on real client engagements, gaining early exposure to professional security consulting
    • Attend internal presales and delivery meetings to learn how GuidePoint scopes, sells, and delivers solutions
    • Practice explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences in client-facing settings under mentorship
    • Support the preparation of presales materials, demos, and technical discussions alongside the Heartland team
  • Technical Writing & Vendor Knowledge
    • Practice technical writing, including executive summaries and findings reports
    • Build vendor-specific product knowledge aligned to GuidePoint's technology partnerships
    • Research and document how partner solutions map to common client security challenges
    • Document lab work, engagement observations, and lessons learned to support your own growth and the team's knowledge base

Qualifications

  • Pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field. Associate's degree candidates with self-study and lab work, and non-traditional backgrounds with equivalent knowledge, will be considered
  • Foundational knowledge of networking, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, HTTP/S, subnetting, VLANs, firewalls, and routing basics
  • Exemplifying leadership tendencies, such as leading student organizations or industry clubs
  • Comfort navigating both Windows and Linux, with command-line proficiency
  • Understanding of core security concepts, including the CIA triad, authentication vs. authorization, encryption basics, and common attack vectors (phishing, malware, ransomware, social engineering)
  • Basic understanding of at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and the shared responsibility model
  • A habit of self-directed learning, shown through home labs, CTFs, blogs, or personal projects
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences
  • Coachable and open to feedback. You don't need to be right, you need to get it right.
  • A self-starter who looks for work without being told, and has a collaborative, team-oriented mindset
  • Professional maturity: punctual, reliable, responsive, and presentable in client-facing settings

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active participation in cybersecurity communities (meetups, BSides, DEFCON, Discord/Slack groups)
  • Any existing certifications (CompTIA ITF+, A+, Network+, Security+)
  • Exposure to a SIEM, vulnerability scanner, or endpoint security tool, even in a lab environment
  • Basic scripting ability (Python, PowerShell, or Bash)
  • Previous customer-facing experience of any kind (retail, help desk, tutoring, etc.)

Internship Details and Expectations

This is a part-time, remote paid internship ($20/hr) that runs for 12 weeks from January 11 - April 2, 2027, with an optional in-person onboarding in Tampa FL during the first week. There is the potential for full-time employment at the end of the internship. During this internship, interns are expected to:

  • Be located near Tulsa, OK, or be willing to relocate there for follow-on full-time hire
  • Be physically located within the United States for the entire internship
  • Work 20-29 hrs/wk during standard business hours supporting the Central Time Zone
  • Have a personal computing device and high-speed internet access during working hours

This position is not available for candidates living in the following states: Alaska, California, Hawaii, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Washington and Wyoming.

The below perks are for those that join GuidePoint Security for full-time employment only.

We use Greenhouse Software as our applicant tracking system and Zoom Scheduler for HR screen request scheduling. At times, your email may block our communication with you. Please be sure to check your SPAM folder so that you don't miss updates on your application.

Why GuidePoint?

GuidePoint Security is a rapidly growing, profitable, privately-held value added reseller that focuses exclusively on Information Security. Since its inception in 2011, GuidePoint has grown to over 1,300 employees, established strategic partnerships with leading security vendors, and serves as a trusted advisor to more than 6,200 customers.

Firmly-defined core values drive all aspects of the business, which have been paramount to the company’s success and establishment of an enjoyable workplace atmosphere. At GuidePoint, your colleagues are knowledgeable, skilled, and experienced and will seek to collaborate and provide mentorship and guidance at every opportunity.

This is a unique and rare opportunity to grow your career along with one of the fastest growing companies in the nation.

Some added perks….

If you choose the High Deductible / HSA plan, GPS will contribute in 4 equal quarterly installments: ($850 per EE annually / $1750 per family annually (includes spouse/children/family options)

Capio Group is a California-based Information Technology Consulting firm serving the public sector since 2010. We assist the Government in delivering large, complex systems and solutions. Capio Group is a small, but quickly growing firm that mixes good ideas, with great people, to achieve extraordinary results for our clients. We offer the salary and benefits of the bigger companies, with the added bonus of a flexible workplace and a great work-life balance.

Scope of Work:

Capio Group is seeking an experienced Functional Lead to work as part of a team on the technical architecture, solution design, security, integration, and configuration strategy for a large-scale public-sector cannabis licensing platform. Functional Lead is responsible for translating complex government cannabis licensing regulations and operational business processes into functional requirements, configurable workflows, and system capabilities. This Functional Lead will serve as the primary bridge between business stakeholders and technical implementation teams, with particular emphasis on licensing, permitting, compliance inspections, enforcement case management, accounts receivable, and user acceptance testing.

The Functional Lead will be responsible for tasks including but not limited to:

  • Business Process Analysis: Lead discovery workshops, analyze existing business processes, identify operational gaps, and define future-state workflows.
  • Licensing Workflow Configuration: Translate cannabis licensing ordinances, multi-division approval processes, ownership hierarchy requirements, license amendments, and regulatory conditions into actionable system configurations.
  • Compliance and Enforcement: Lead functional design for compliance management, inspection scheduling, mobile field inspections, violations, enforcement cases, and related regulatory workflows.
  • Functional Requirements: Develop and validate requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, business process maps, configuration specifications, and traceability documentation.
  • Accounts Receivable: Define functional requirements for fee assessment, invoicing, payment workflows, aging reports, financial adjustments, waivers, and approval processes.
  • Financial Controls: Establish functional requirements addressing separation of duties, auditability, financial reporting, and internal control considerations.
  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Facilitate sessions with DCR SMEs, licensing staff, inspection personnel, enforcement teams, finance staff, and other City stakeholders.
  • User Acceptance Testing: Coordinate UAT planning, scenario development, business rule verification, defect resolution, and functional acceptance.
  • Reporting and Analytics: Define operational, licensing, inspection, enforcement, financial, and audit reporting requirements.
  • Training and Transition: Support training teams with functional documentation, realistic business scenarios, and knowledge transfer.

Mandatory Experience:

  1. Must have minimum three (3) years of relevant experience supporting a government organization with an annual operating budget of at least $1 billion or serving a population of at least 900,000 residents.
  2. Must have minimum three (3) years of experience with similar Salesforce solutions in a jurisdiction that utilized permitting, inspections, and code enforcement capabilities.
  3. Must have minimum three (3) years of demonstrated experience for oversight of Salesforce functional implementation activities, including requirements, business workflows, system configuration, functional testing, and acceptance.
  4. Within the past five (5) years, must have demonstrated experience leading at least one enterprise system implementation for a large government entity utilizing a Salesforce solution or Salesforce development ecosystem.
  5. Must have minimum three (3) years of experience with public-sector jurisdictions currently using a product designed specifically for commercial cannabis licensing, including translating unique cannabis ordinances and social equity rules into standard system configurations and implementation best practices.
  6. Must have minimum three (3) years of experience implementing configuration-first or metadata driven, low-code cannabis licensing software platforms for public-sector agencies, including typical scale, duration, and complexity of such implementations.
  7. Must have minimum three (3) years of experience leading data migration projects from legacy or heavily customized systems.
  8. Must have minimum three (3) years of relevant experience providing platforms with an API-first that securely orchestrates data exchanges with external systems, payment gateways, enterprise financial systems, document repositories, and enterprise Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
  9. Must have minimum three (3) years of experience providing operational support and training for public-sector licensing systems, including support for end-users, system administrators, and technical staff.
  10. Must have three (3) years of experience with supporting accounts receivable functions for public-sector licensing or regulatory programs.
  11. Must have familiarity with audit, internal control, and separation-of duties requirements common to local governments.
  12. Must have minimum three (3) years of experience providing reporting and analytics tools for public-sector licensing or regulatory systems, including audit, financial, or operational reporting.

Director, Data Science - Consumer and Developer Experience (Remote-Eligible)

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.


As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.


Team Description

At Capital One, we are relentless innovators with a proven track record of transforming customers’ experiences and the financial services industry. We’re delivering best-in-class innovation so that our more than 100 million customers can manage their finances with ease.


We consider ourselves the bank a technology company would build – empowered to use artificial intelligence (from machine learning to generative AI) to transform everyday banking into real-time, intelligent products that help customers improve their financial well-being. We’re all-in on the cloud and are a leader in the adoption of open source. We build our own products and release them with a speed and agility that allows us to get new customer experiences to market quickly. We’re going boldly where no bank has gone before. And, as a founder-led company, we are centered in our mission to help customers succeed.


The Role | General Responsibilities:


We’re seeking a Data Science Manager to support strategic priorities for Consumer and Developer Experience (CDX), as part of CDX’s product strategy team. CDX is an exciting space with diverse product responsibilities. The organization’s remit spans customer digital engagement, including the Capital One app; Capital One’s marketing platform, analytics, and personalization engine; the product suite used to manage all Capital One suppliers and vendors; products associated with the company’s risk management responsibilities; and more.


CDX’s product strategy team is a blend of strategy, product, and data science. We tackle the organization’s hardest strategic and analytical questions, delivering answers that fundamentally change the way we do business. We also act as an innovation lab, developing prototypes and partnering closely with product and engineering teams to translate conceptual visions into tangible, scaled digital experiences. We are looking for someone who thrives in this duality – someone who is equally energized by big-picture questions about where the world is going, thorny problems that require a strategic mindset and deep analytical rigor, and hands-on building.


In this role, you will:

  • Partner with a cross-functional team of software engineers, business analysts, and product managers to ensure we are delivering products customers love that move the needle for the business
  • Leverage a broad stack of technologies - Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more - to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data
  • Build machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation
  • Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

The Ideal Candidate is:

  • Customer first. You love the process of analyzing and creating, but also share our passion to do the right thing. You know at the end of the day it’s about making the right decision for our customers.
  • Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.
  • A leader. You challenge conventional thinking and work with stakeholders to identify and improve the status quo. You’re passionate about talent development for your own team and beyond.
  • Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.
  • Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning.
  • A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:
    • A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 9 years of experience performing data analytics
    • A Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration plus 7 years of experience performing data analytics
    • A PHD in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 4 years of experience performing data analytics
  • At least 4 years of experience leveraging open source programming languages for large scale data analysis
  • At least 4 years of experience working with machine learning
  • At least 4 years of experience utilizing relational databases

Preferred Qualifications:

  • PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) plus 5 years of experience in data analytics
  • At least 1 year of experience working with AWS
  • At least 3 year of experience managing people
  • At least 5 years of experience in Python, Scala, or R for large scale data analysis
  • At least 5 years of experience with machine learning
